original_question: Which compact symmetric spaces of group type, without assuming simple connectivity, admit manifold quotients that are isospectral but not isometric?
target_in_paper: Question 7.6: Which compact symmetric spaces of group type (not necessarily simply connected) cover isospectral manifolds.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly singles out the group-type case, correctly removes the simple-connectivity assumption in the same spirit as Question 7.6, and correctly asks for a classification by existence of quotient manifolds that are isospectral but not isometric.
missing_details: The exact target is Question 7.6 in Section 7, not the broader Question 1.15.

In Section 7, the authors explicitly adopt the convention that they will omit the words 'and non-isometric' when speaking of manifolds covered by a symmetric space; a stand-alone formulation should restore that condition.
The relevant class is the compact irreducible symmetric spaces of group type, described there as X = (K x K)/diag(K) with K a compact simple Lie group.
The paper also uses the equivalent concrete model X isometric to K endowed with a bi-invariant metric; stating this makes the question self-contained.
The quotients in question are compact manifold quotients obtained via finite free isometric actions, equivalently finite Riemannian covering maps X -> M_i.
Isospectrality here means equality of the Laplace-Beltrami spectra on functions, counted with multiplicities.
If one writes the question in the Lie-group model, the quotient metrics on K/Gamma_i are the metrics induced from the chosen bi-invariant metric, as in Proposition 7.4.
refined_question: Determine exactly which compact irreducible symmetric spaces of group type X = (K x K)/diag(K), where K is a compact connected simple Lie group and X is not assumed simply connected, admit two compact manifold quotients M1 and M2 covered by X via finite Riemannian covering maps such that M1 and M2 are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions, counted with multiplicities, but are not isometric.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for which compact connected simple Lie groups K endowed with a bi-invariant metric g0 do there exist finite subgroups Gamma1, Gamma2 acting freely by isometries on K such that the induced quotient manifolds (K/Gamma1, g1) and (K/Gamma2, g2) are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?
justification: The draft is aiming at Question 7.6 almost verbatim. The nearby context in Section 7 explains that the section is about symmetric spaces that cover isospectral and non-isometric manifolds, then narrows to the group-type case and identifies such spaces with compact simple Lie groups carrying bi-invariant metrics. Proposition 7.4 gives the concrete quotient model by finite subgroups, while Theorem 1.16 supplies the nearby partial classification that motivates the remaining open classification problem.
